What it costs

Graduated per lot, per month, like a tax bracket: $2.50 each for the first 10 lots, $1.10 for lots 11 to 70, $0.40 for every lot above 70, with a $10 monthly minimum. A four-lot association pays $10 a month; a 100-lot association pays $103; a 1,000-lot association pays $463. Everything is included: collections, violations, elections, vendor management, documents and the audit trail, with no feature tiers and no per-notice charge. Owners pay no fee to pay their dues. Billing is month to month with no contract, no setup fee, and a full export of ledgers, documents, minutes and audit trail available in any month, including the month an association leaves.

Frequently asked questions

Where does our dues money actually go?

Into the association's own account, in the association's own name, at the association's own bank. Owners pay it directly; Parcel is not in that line and has no way to move a dollar out of it.

Can the software send a lien or a fine on its own?

No. A lien, a fine or a statutory notice requires two officers to sign. There is no way to approve a batch, and no way for software to sign on a board's behalf.

What if it cites a rule our documents don't contain?

It won't. If Parcel cannot point at the page and the line in your own documents, it prints a dash and tells you why, so any letter you send is one you can defend.

What is HOA management software, and what does Common Parcel actually do?

HOA management software runs the recurring work of a homeowners association: dues invoicing and collection, delinquency notices, violations, architectural review, vendor contracts, elections, meeting minutes and record-keeping. Common Parcel does that work automatically from your own governing documents, and stops for a board signature only where the law or the money requires a person.

Can a self-managed HOA run without a property management company?

Yes. Most associations under a few hundred doors are self-managed, and the work that used to justify a management company is exactly the work software now does: invoicing dues, sending notices, tracking deadlines, collecting bids. Boards keep the decisions; Parcel does the labor and keeps the audit trail.

How much does HOA management software cost?

Common Parcel is priced per door on a sliding scale that drops as the association grows: $12.50 a month at five units, $103 a month for a hundred-home association, and about 46 cents per door at a thousand. Everything is included: no per-feature tiers, and no payment-processing upcharge to the association.

How does Common Parcel compare with other HOA platforms?

Most HOA platforms give you tools and expect a volunteer to operate them: you still set up the rules, remember the deadlines and write the notices. Common Parcel reads your CC&Rs and bylaws, configures itself, and runs the month unattended, with collections, violations, voting and vendor management in one price.

How do homeowners pay HOA dues online?

Owners pay by autopay, one-time card or ACH bank transfer, and mailed checks are logged against the right lot. Receipts post the same day, ledgers reconcile nightly, and no volunteer treasurer has to visit a bank.

Does it handle violation tracking and architectural review requests?

Yes. Violations are logged with photo, date and the provision they breach; courtesy notices, cure windows, re-inspections and hearing deadlines run on schedule. Architectural requests carry the statutory response clock, and the board's decision and reasoning are written to the record.

Can we run board elections and proxy voting online?

Yes. Electronic ballots and proxies where your state permits them, with paper ballots logged alongside. Quorum is tracked live against your bylaws' threshold, meeting notices go out on the statutory schedule, and minutes are drafted the moment the vote closes.

What about HOA accounting, budgets and financial reports?

Every payment, fee and vendor invoice lands in the ledger with its receipt. Monthly financials, budget-versus-actual, delinquency reports and the full audit trail export to your accountant or auditor whenever you ask.

Do we have to type our CC&Rs and bylaws into the system?

No. Upload the declaration, bylaws, rules and roster, and Parcel reads them, pulling out the assessment amount, due dates, grace period, late fee, and meeting and voting rules, then shows you each one with the page and line it came from. You confirm what it read; anything it cannot find prints as unknown rather than a guess. Setup usually takes about thirty minutes.

Does this work for condo associations and civic or neighborhood associations?

Yes. It runs condominium associations, planned communities and HOAs of five to a thousand-plus doors, and civic, neighborhood and block associations, which carry lighter statutory obligations.

How do we switch from our current management company?

Parcel prepares the termination notice your contract requires, the records request, and a thirty-day transition checklist, then loads the ledgers, documents and roster you receive. There is no charge for the migration.

Who owns the data, and can we leave?

Your association's records are yours. Billing is month to month, and a full export of ledgers, documents, minutes and the audit trail is available any month, including the month you leave.

In more detail

Common Parcel is HOA management software for self-managed homeowners associations, condominium associations, planned communities, and civic or neighbourhood associations in the United States. It is built for volunteer boards that run the association themselves, without a property management company, a bookkeeper, or a designated software person.

What it does

A board uploads its declaration, bylaws, rules and owner roster. Common Parcel reads those documents and extracts the numbers that govern everything else: the assessment amount, the due date, the grace period, the late fee, and the meeting and voting rules. It shows each one with the page and line it came from. From then on it runs the association's recurring work on the schedule those documents and the relevant state statute already set: it invoices dues, collects them by autopay, ACH or card, posts receipts to owner ledgers, reconciles the bank, applies late fees, issues the delinquency ladder of reminder, demand and lien, logs violations with photo and citation, runs cure windows and re-inspections, carries architectural review requests on their statutory response clock, tracks vendor contracts and re-bids them before they renew, runs elections with electronic ballots and proxies, tracks quorum, drafts minutes, and writes every action to a numbered audit trail.

What the board still does

Anything with legal or financial weight stops for a person. A lien, a fine, or a statutory notice requires two officers to sign; there is no batch approval and no way for the software to sign on the board's behalf. A typical month leaves the board two decisions and about twenty-two minutes of work.

Custody of funds

Owners pay into the association's own bank account, in the association's own name. Common Parcel is not in that payment path and has no ability to move association money.

Citations

Every notice quotes the provision, page and line it came from. If Common Parcel cannot locate the governing provision, it prints a dash and says so rather than inventing a citation.

Comparison

Common Parcel configures itself from the association's own documents and runs the month unattended.

Migration

Common Parcel prepares the termination notice an existing management contract requires, the records request, and a thirty-day transition checklist, then loads the ledgers, documents and roster the association receives. There is no charge for migration.

Status and availability

Common Parcel is onboarding founding associations now. It is built in Michigan and accepts associations anywhere in the United States.
